theory.intro: The triangle area formula $A = \tfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$ can be rearranged to find an unknown side or included angle when the area is known. For positive side lengths, solving for an angle gives two supplementary solutions when $0 < \dfrac{2A}{ab} < 1$, the single angle $90^{\circ}$ when the ratio equals $1$, and no possible triangle when the ratio is greater than $1$.
facts: To find an unknown side length, rearrange the area formula to $b = \dfrac{2A}{a\sin C}$.
To find the included angle, rearrange the area formula to $\sin C = \dfrac{2A}{ab}$.
Because $\sin C = \sin(180^{\circ} - C)$, there are two supplementary angle solutions when $0 < \dfrac{2A}{ab} < 1$: acute $C$ and obtuse $180^{\circ} - C$.
If the question or diagram specifies whether the included angle is acute or obtuse, give only that single angle.

If no angle type is specified and $0 < \dfrac{2A}{ab} < 1$, both supplementary angles are valid. If the ratio equals $1$, the only included angle is $90^{\circ}$; if it is greater than $1$ or non-positive, no non-degenerate triangle is possible.
For an isosceles triangle with equal sides $x$ and included angle $C$, each side is $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{2A}{\sin C}}$.
steps: Substitute the known area, side lengths, and angle
Rearrange and solve for the unknown side or angle

State the side length or the angle selected by the question or diagram; for an unrestricted angle, give both supplementary solutions when the sine ratio lies between $0$ and $1$, $90^{\circ}$ when it equals $1$, or no possible triangle when it exceeds $1$ or is non-positive

foundation.question_text:
A triangle has an area of $36\text{ cm}^{2}$, a side of length $9\text{ cm}$, and an included angle of $30^{\circ}$.
Find the length of the other side forming this angle.

A triangle has an area of $42\text{ m}^{2}$.
Two of its sides meet at an obtuse angle of $120^{\circ}$, and one of those sides is $14\text{ m}$ long.
Find the length of the other side, correct to $1$ decimal place.

A triangle has sides of $8\text{ cm}$ and $11\text{ cm}$ and an area of $22\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is acute, find $\theta$ to the nearest degree.

A triangle has sides of length $6\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$ and an area of $15\text{ m}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is obtuse, find $\theta$ to the nearest degree.

A triangle has sides of $8\text{ cm}$ and $14\text{ cm}$ and an area of $28\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is acute, find $\theta$ to the nearest minute.

development.question_text:
A triangular solar panel has an area of $1.8\text{ m}^{2}$.
One edge is $2.4\text{ m}$ long and makes an angle of $52^{\circ}$ with an adjacent edge.
Find the length of the adjacent edge, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A triangular roof gable has an area of $15.6\text{ m}^{2}$.
Two timber rafters meet at an obtuse ridge angle of $118^{\circ}$.
If one rafter is $5.8\text{ m}$ long, calculate the length of the other rafter, correct to $2$ decimal places.

Two straight boundaries of a triangular plot measure $40\text{ m}$ and $70\text{ m}$, and the plot has an area of $700\text{ m}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is acute, find $\theta$ to the nearest minute.

An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of $40^{\circ}$ and an area of $50\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Find the length of each of the two equal sides, correct to $2$ decimal places.

mastery.question_text:
An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles of $72^{\circ}$ and an area of $84\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Find the length of each of the two equal sides, correct to $2$ decimal places.

A triangle has sides of length $5\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$, and its area is $30\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Given that the included angle $\theta$ is acute, find $\theta$ to the nearest degree.

An isosceles triangle has an apex angle of $60^{\circ}$ and an area of $27\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^{2}$.
Find the length of each of the two equal sides, correct to $2$ decimal places.
